dual_runtime_contract.readme: Two interchangeable core implementations are deliberately retained for redundancy and parity
dual_runtime_contract.contract_invariant: python and rust cores expose the same required ownership commands
dual_runtime_contract.recent_explicit_preservation: regression-research#400 merged 2026-09-03 and explicitly preserved dual Python/Rust implementations
dual_runtime_contract.bounded_fallback_search_result: No issue/report match found for busy-rust fallback/recovery from Python failure; this is negative bounded evidence, not proof of absence.

maintenance_history.interpretation: Every current-history core change was implemented in both languages; duplicated maintenance is contract-enforced rather than occasional.

live_parity_control.operation: snapshot --limit 32 against the same canonical store
live_parity_control.note: A first sequential 8-item byte comparison differed because the store changed between reads; a subsequent structural comparison at limit 32 returned zero semantic differences.

installed_footprint.interpretation: ~101.5 MB is Cargo target/build cache and is not required runtime payload; do not count it as architectural savings. The installed Rust runtime/source payload itself is ~767 KB.

candidate_remove: dual-runtime parity invariant and parity-only verification after replacement acceptance
classification.candidate_replacement: One Python Busy core remains the single coordinator implementation; retain the same store/schema/safety behavior. Do not add another fallback service.
required_before_mutation: verify no current production consumer depends on busy-rust entrypoint
positive safety replay covering claim/heartbeat/release/recover/sweep and Windows store contention with Python-only install

caveats: Current structured MCP timeline does not retain launched command strings, so it cannot prove zero recent rust invocations.
No running/scheduled rust consumer and no bounded fallback/recovery documentation were observed; absence is not universal proof.
The local Vault checkout HEAD is behind origin/main; serving install matches origin/main modulo CRLF, so measurements use origin/main for source counts.
